chunks: When Our lucid revelations are read out to them, the infidels say to those who believe: 'Which of the two groups is better in standing, and whose company is more excellent?'
ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers ask the believers when Quranic verses were recited to them?
ai.summary: In Surah Maryam, this verse captures the disbelievers' pragmatic critique of the early Muslims, contrasting their perceived worldly weakness with the believers' spiritual conviction. Shia exegesis often highlights this as a recurring theme where material success is mistaken for divine favor, a concept echoed in the 'good life' (hayat tayyibah) promised to the righteous. The rhetorical question underscores the tension between temporal power and eternal truth, a central motif in Quranic discourse on faith.
